tokyo_istanbul_ginza_corridor.notes: [Turkish · Corridor-gai since 1988] A 44-seat Turkish restaurant on Corridor Street (8 counter seats, the rest tables) that bills itself as Japan's first, established in 1988, with a Turkish chef. Cooking is spiced rather than hot. Groups order the meze platter with pita (a spinach dish stands out), cheese-filled spring rolls and spinach crêpes, then a kebab assortment of beef, chicken, lamb and minced meat, or doner and lamb shish. Butter rice and salad come alongside. Baklava and pistachio paste are flown in through a partnership with the Istanbul sweets house Güllüoğlu, best with Turkish coffee. Efes beer, Turkish wine and pomegranate juice. The daily lunch, such as beef-salami sausage with potato stew, is under ¥1,500; free-flow courses start at ¥5,500.

tokyo_le_nougat_ginza6.notes: [French bistro · à la carte] A Paris street-corner bistro of 44 seats, open since 2008, with antique decor, a terrace-like ground floor and a high-ceilinged upper room dotted with elephant ornaments. People queue before the 5 p.m. opening and it fills within half an hour, so groups of three or more should book early. Many guests are from overseas. You order à la carte from the grand menu and a chalkboard of specials. The popular carrot rémoulade comes first, then mushroom and watercress salad, sakura-meat tartare, bouillabaisse, sautéed Spanish mackerel, cassoulet (a full order serves four), rabbit with mustard sauce, Ezo venison en croûte, bear in season and an Okukuji-egg herb omurice. Portions are generous, so don't over-order. A thick wine list; 10% service charge. One reviewer notes it has held a Michelin Bib Gourmand.

tokyo_tutto_il_mare_ginza4.notes: [Sicilian · behind the Kabuki-za] A 48-seat Sicilian restaurant over two floors of a small pink house behind the Kabuki-za, open since 2013. It is a branch: Tabelog notes the main shop has been listed as a Michelin Bib Gourmand. The specialty is homemade busiate (twisted pasta) in a rich red-shrimp sauce, alongside Trapani-style seafood couscous. Weekday lunch sets come with focaccia and a big salad: a traditional Sicilian tomato pasta with orange cake, or a lean bistecca with plenty of potatoes. Free-flow party plans with Peroni on draft fill the third floor. One October 2026 diner found the tables cramped and noisy, the service slow and the one-drink rule costly at about ¥800 for a soft drink. ¥400 cover at dinner.

chef_bio.background: Multi-shop group; main shop listed Bib Gourmand per Tabelog.

tokyo_ginza_zion_ginza5.notes: [Italian bar · parties a minute from Ginza Station] A 48-seat basement Italian bar with café-style sofa seating, built for welcome, farewell and birthday parties, with projector and microphone. Courses with two-hour free-flow cost about ¥5,000, with grilled black Wagyu, a seafood paella diners rate, chewy-crust pizza such as quattro formaggi, and a Camembert and mentaiko ajillo. Free-flow drinks are basic: one diner found only Asahi Super Dry and a weak highball. There is a single restroom, and large groups can make it hot and loud. ¥600 appetizer and 10% service.

tokyo_vidrio_mitsukoshi_ginza4.notes: [Spanish · paella on the Mitsukoshi restaurant floor] The Ginza Mitsukoshi branch of VIDRIO (びいどろ), a Spanish restaurant whose paellas have won a Tokyo paella competition and an international Valencia-paella prize, and whose fideuà won in Gandia. The 48-seat room is modelled on the port town of Gandia, with comfortable spacing and semi-private areas. Paella comes in individual pans, so two people can share different ones, such as seafood and squid ink. The weekend set adds a tapas platter, ajillo, dessert and coffee. À la carte, 2026 diners liked marinated sardines with gari, Galician-style scallops, a sea-urchin and ikura gratin, a mushroom ajillo, a truffle potato galette and fried squid. Mitsukoshi points can't be used.

You can order à la carte and have it served like a course. 2026 diners praise the caviar capellini, sea-urchin pasta, a white-fish main, sirloin steak and the Basque cheesecake. The lunch course lets two people share different pastas and mains. Also open for breakfast. About ¥8,000–10,000 at lunch and ¥15,000–30,000 at dinner; 10% service, plus ¥1,000 a head after 9 p.m.

tokyo_drape_tokyo_kaikan_hibiya.notes: [French café · Tokyo Kaikan at Hibiya] A bright, big-windowed 52-seat café-brasserie (12 at the counter) run by Tokyo Kaikan, open since 2023 and all day from 11:00. A weekend lunch course runs salad-style hors d'oeuvres with herring, pork fillet in Marsala sauce and an assorted dessert plate. The drinks list is long, with plenty of non-alcoholic choices and a pretty house soda. Service carries Tokyo Kaikan's standards. Two-hour limit when busy.

It has cushioned sofa nooks and loft-style private rooms for two to eight, though the ceiling is low. Lunch courses (five dishes, about ¥1,000–3,000) are reservation-heavy and fully booked at peak. The draw is the seafood paella, heaped with large shrimp, crab and mussels and finished with lemon, plus a hot shrimp ajillo with baguette and a balsamic salad. Dinner adds a sparkling-wine free-flow course, and there are plenty of non-alcoholic drinks. Staff are quick and kind.

Some October 2026 diners found the staff brusque and one found the pasta dry.

tokyo_susans_meatball_hibiya.notes: [American · meatballs in the Midtown Hibiya food hall] A 56-seat counter in the HIBIYA FOOD HALL under Tokyo Midtown Hibiya, right by the lifts from the TOHO cinema, with its own seats plus the hall's shared ones. Open since 2018. Choose beef, pork or basil-chicken meatballs, or one of each, over pasta, rice or bread with fries or mash. Pasta sauces are tomato, chili, mushroom cream or spicy mala tomato. In 2026 the meatball pasta cost ¥1,000, a meatball burger ¥1,050 and the cheese version ¥1,100, with Carlsberg at ¥650. Diners rate the pork meatballs fluffiest. Good before or between films.

chef_bio.background: Food-hall counter; no source names the operator.

anecdotes.text: "I had the meatball pasta a la carte for exactly JPY 1000! You can choose three meatballs from beef, pork, and basil chicken… the pork was the fluffiest." — October 2026.
"For the pasta sauce, you can select from tomato sauce, chili sauce, mushroom cream sauce, or spicy mala tomato sauce." — October 2026.

tokyo_hola_ginza7.notes: [Spanish bar · Ginza 7-chōme, smoking allowed] A 60-seat Spanish bar near Shimbashi, open since 2012, for parties, day drinking and late Fridays (to 4 a.m.). The signature is angel-shrimp paella, or you can choose your own ingredients for a custom paella, served about 20 minutes after ordering. Also pinchos, prosciutto, ajillo, sangria by the decanter and fresh cider, plus a paella and salad lunch set. Staff are friendly; a tip-based table magician appeared one October night. Note that smoking is allowed at every seat, and one diner found prices high, likely due to the location. About ¥5,000–8,000 at dinner.

tokyo_osteria_da_ada_ginza6.notes: [Italian · standing bar and dining room] A lively fourth-floor osteria that opens straight off the lift into a standing bar, with a calmer 16-seat dining room at the back, open since 2019. The standing counter takes no bookings and is lunch's only option. Wine is cheap for Ginza: glasses from ¥300 to ¥900, generously poured. Counter appetizers are ¥300–450 each, and pastas about ¥1,500. 2026 diners rate the bonito and sweet-shrimp carpaccio, the seafood platter, clams in white wine, prosciutto, a colourful vegetable appetizer, lemon pasta and tiramisu. It's full by 7 p.m. on Saturdays. About ¥4,000–8,000 a head.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 16 November 2019 (Tabelog); a sister shop in Shinjuku (2026 review)

tokyo_lavasara_ginza2.notes: [Italian · café and grill on the 11th floor] A bright 63-seat Italian café and grill on the 11th floor of Marronnier Gate Ginza 1, open since May 2025, with open views, families welcome and many overseas customers. You order by QR code. Lunch sets with pizza or pasta (such as squid ink) include free soft-drink refills. À la carte, diners had burrata and prosciutto salad, grilled vegetables, Bolognese, Margherita pizza and a chocolate terrine, served one at a time like a course. Friendly service, but reviewers call the flavours ordinary and à la carte pricey. 10% service after 5 p.m.

chef_bio.background: No source names the operator.
chef_bio.philosophy: Warm but not over-formal service (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "We had a salad with burrata cheese and prosciutto, grilled vegetables, and a Bolognese dish. I appreciated that the dishes were served one by one, like a course meal." — October 2026.
"I appreciated the unlimited soft drinks; it's a nice option for when you want to relax and chat." — October 2026, lunch set.

tokyo_la_scene_mercure_hibiya.notes: [French · hotel lounge at Mercure Tokyo Hibiya] The all-day restaurant, café and bar of the Mercure Tokyo Hibiya, open since December 2023. Its 77 seats are spread over sofas, tables, a private room and a semi-private room in a basement that still gets natural light, and you can reach it underground from Shimbashi without getting rained on. Surprisingly quiet for Shimbashi. The weekend lunch set includes a drink, a choice of four appetizers and a fish, meat or pasta main, with unlimited bread. Tea-time regulars come for the seasonal fruit tart, with a crisp crust, and flavoured teas such as mango-strawberry. Truffle fries are on the bar menu. Staff were kind even to a diner in sweatpants. Tabelog lists allergy information and vegetarian options.

chef_bio.background: Hotel restaurant (Mercure Tokyo Hibiya).

anecdotes.text: "For the appetizers, I could choose from four options, and for the main dish, I selected one from fish, meat, or pasta… the unlimited bread helped make it a satisfying meal." — August 2026.
"I was in my natural state with no makeup and dressed in what looked like sweatpants, but the staff treated me with kindness and courtesy." — September 2026.

tokyo_el_chateo_ginza3.notes: [Spanish · paella wine bar by Ginza Station] A busy 78-seat Spanish wine bar over two floors, a minute from Ginza Station, open since 1996. It carries on the home cooking of the VIDRIO (びいどろ) group, whose paella has twice won at the Spanish world championship. Tapas start at ¥500. Lunch sets pair a paella, such as seafood, squid ink with mayonnaise sauce, or duck breast and truffle mushroom, with an assorted tapas plate and a drink. A ¥3,850 lunch course adds steak. Paella takes time, so book or expect a short wait. Dinner courses of eight dishes with two-hour free-flow start at ¥6,600; ¥550 dinner charge otherwise.

chef_bio.background: Group-run (juraku.com, sister of VIDRIO).

anecdotes.text: "The squid ink paella had a perfect balance of squid ink flavor and mayonnaise sauce, with an exquisite cooking texture." — October 2026, lunch.
"Lunch course + 2 Maou Beers, JPY 3,850 + JPY 1,980… The appetizers were plentiful, and the steak was delicious." — October 2026.
